exposure: Mode of delivery (elective caesarean delivery, vaginal breech delivery)
cohort: 1,774 women who delivered a singleton fetus in breech position from 32 weeks' gestation onwards between January 2011 and December 2017 at a single center
finding: While a high rate of successful vaginal breech deliveries occurred after planned vaginal breech delivery, compromised neonatal outcome at term was more frequent in the planned vaginal breech delivery group compared to the elective caesarean delivery group.
mod_finding: Neonatal morbidity at term was significantly higher in the planned vaginal breech delivery group compared to the elective caesarean delivery group (12% vs 4%), while severe maternal postpartum complications were more frequent in the elective caesarean delivery group compared to the successful vaginal breech delivery group (2% vs 0.3%).
